text: Rollback DSU with parity; bipartite at every moment.

A rollback DSU (可撤销并查集) undoes its last merges in reverse order. Use union by size (or rank) only, no path compression, so a merge changes just two values: the parent of the smaller root and the size of the larger. Push those changes on a stack; undo pops them. find is O(log n).

Path compression rewrites many parents in one find, which cannot be undone cheaply; union by size alone keeps trees O(log n) deep. A DSU that also stores the parity to the root (weighted DSU) can check bipartiteness: joining two nodes of the same parity in the same component means an odd cycle.

Segment tree on time (线段树分治) solves offline problems where items (edges, values) exist during a time interval and queries ask about each moment. Put each item into the O(log T) segment-tree nodes that cover its interval. DFS the tree: entering a node, add its items (merges in the rollback DSU); at a leaf, answer that moment; leaving, roll back.

Deletion is the hard operation for DSU; this trick needs only "add" and "undo the last add". Total cost O(m log T log n). It also works with linear bases, knapsacks, or anything that can be undone in order.

Is the graph bipartite at each moment (P5787)? Each edge lives during (l, r]. The answers for random edges are checked by colouring each moment's graph in Python. Once an odd cycle appears in a node, every moment below it is "No", so the flag is passed down and further merges are skipped.
Do not add path compression "for speed": it breaks rollback. Roll back to the stack size you saw on entering the node, not by a count of merges, because a failed or skipped merge pushes nothing.

Related: a persistent DSU (P3402) keeps every version with a persistent array (进阶篇第8章) for fa and size, again without path compression. Offline dynamic connectivity (P2147 without LCT) is segment tree on time with a plain rollback DSU.
